subject: FinApps \u0014 Tool calling integration patterns (post-call recap & next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: FinApps  Tool calling integration patterns (post-call recap & next steps)

Thanks again for the call today, Sarah - great to meet the FinApps engineering team and hear more about your payments reconciliation use case. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can align the architecture review.

Recap of needs we heard:
- Low-latency enrichment of transactions (100-300ms per API call target for the UI path).
- Multiple external actions from the model: 1) lookup customer account, 2) call tax-rate calc service, 3) create a reconciliation ticket. Some actions can be parallel; others are dependent.
- Robust error handling and observability for each tool call (idempotency, retries, fallbacks).
- Re-ranker over embeddings for candidate retrieval before generation.

High-level patterns we recommend:
- SDK setup & auth: we can support API-key headers for hosted, OAuth client-credentials for integrations, and mTLS for Private deployments. The SDK quickstart I attached includes examples for Node/Python.
- Routing & model choice: route short interactive UI calls to our low-latency model variant; route batch/async workflows to higher-throughput variants. Use request-level routing by intent + size.
- Structured output & function/tool calling: define tools as typed JSON schema (name, input_schema, idempotency, timeout_ms, scopes). Prefer explicit output schema to avoid brittle NLU parsing.
- Tool definitions & parallelism: run independent, read-only tools in parallel up to a configured concurrency; sequence dependent writes after successful reads. When running parallel tools, use a race-with-quorum approach and explicit timeouts (e.g., 200ms for non-critical reads).
- Embeddings & rerankers: embed candidate docs/transactions (dim 1536 typical), use ANN store (FAISS/Pinecone/Milvus), then run a compact reranker model to pick top-K for generation.
- Error handling: circuit breakers per-tool, retry with exponential backoff for idempotent ops, clear fallbacks (return safe message or escalate to human). Instrument per-tool latency and error rates in Console.

Attachments I added:
- rdw-tool-calling-patterns-v1.pdf (pattern reference)
- sdk-quickstart.md (setup snippets for Node/Python)

Proposed next steps:
1) Share a short architecture doc (I attached v1).
2) Schedule an architecture review with your eng + our runtime engineers (Dev) - propose Tue/Wed this week.
3) Define POC success criteria (latency, error budget, accuracy of enrichment).

If you can confirm a preferred time for the architecture sync and attach any network/security constraints (VPC peering, IP allowlists, KMS requirements), we'll prepare a tailored runbook.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@finapps.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FinApps  Tool calling integration patterns (post-call recap & next steps)

Hi Sarah - quick technical answers and a few concrete examples below. Happy to walk through live at the arch sync.

1) Example tool-definition (JSON metadata we recommend storing alongside your integration):
{
  "name": "customer_lookup",
  "description": "Lookup customer by email/ID",
  "input_schema": {"type":"object","properties":{"email":{"type":"string"}},"required":["email"]},
  "idempotent": "true",
  "timeout_ms": "200",
  "retry_policy": "none",
  "scopes": ["read:customers"]
}

For a write operation (e.g., create_ticket): set idempotent=false, include a client-provided idempotency_key and a retry_policy (e.g., backoff up to N attempts).

2) Auth examples we include in sdk-auth-examples.md (attached) - summary here:
- API key (hosted): Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY> header.
- OAuth2 client credentials (sandbox/SSO): standard token endpoint + client_id/secret, token cache in SDK.
- mTLS (private): mutual cert exchange during TLS handshake; SDK supports loading client cert + key and verifying server cert fingerprint. We also expose an option to rotate certs via your KMS.

3) Embedding store guidance:
- For 10s of millions of vectors we recommend a managed ANN service (Pinecone/Milvus/Weaviate) or a sharded FAISS with IVF + PQ.
- Dimensionality: 768-1536 depending on model; higher dims improve recall but increase storage/cost. Normalize vectors; use cosine similarity if normalized.
- Reranker: run a compact cross-encoder on top ~100 candidates (cost/latency tradeoff). Expect rerank step to add ~50-150ms depending on model; you can mitigate by reducing candidate K or using an asymmetric hybrid approach.

4) Latency & parallel tool calls:
- Parallel read-only lookups: run in parallel with per-call timeout (e.g., 150-250ms); overall wall time typically max(timeout) + small merge cost.
- Dependent writes: sequence after successful reads - add a short orchestration hop (10-30ms).
- Overall: UI path with 1 rerank + 2 parallel reads + 1 quick write (seq) can be achievable in ~200-350ms if you size resources and keep reranker lightweight. We'll benchmark with your traffic profile.

Error handling patterns to adopt:
- Timeouts per-tool + fallbacks to cached/stale result for non-critical reads.
- Circuit breaker per remote service and per-tool: open after N failures, short-circuit requests to fallback.
- Validation layer: verify tool outputs against their declared schema; on mismatch, route to human review channel and return deterministic safe response to caller.

I attached sdk-auth-examples.md with code snippets for Node/Python and a sample Postman collection for quick testing.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
